title: Properties of Operations and the Order of Operations
seo_title: Grade 6 Properties and Order of Operations Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise and use the commutative, associative and distributive properties with whole numbers; recognise and use the order of operations, including brackets.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 worksheets: commutative, associative and distributive properties, the order of operations and brackets. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Order and grouping do not change + and ×.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Commutative: 25 + 48 = 48 + 25 and 6 × 9 = 9 × 6. Associative: (4 × 25) × 7 = 4 × (25 × 7).
  • Distributive: 8 × 47 = 8 × 40 + 8 × 7.
  • Order of operations: brackets first, then × and ÷ from left to right, then + and − from left to right.
  • The properties work for + and ×, not for − and ÷.

Examples

Example

20 − 4 × 3 + (6 + 2)

brackets: 8

× : 12

20 − 12 + 8

Answer: 16

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Left to right only× and ÷ come before + and −.
Ignoring bracketsWork out brackets first.
− is not commutative9 − 4 ≠ 4 − 9.

items.q: The second array is the first one turned on its side. Which equation do the two arrays show?
items.e: Turning an array does not add or remove any dots. Both have 24 dots, so 4 × 6 = 6 × 4. This is the commutative property.

items.q: Which grouping of 2 × 8 × 5 makes a 10 first?
items.e: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 × 8 = 80 is easy. The other groupings with × give the same product, but with harder steps. (2 + 5) × 8 adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: Which grouping of 5 × 3 × 2 makes a 10 first?
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, and 10 × 3 = 30 is easy. The other groupings with × give the same product, but with harder steps. (5 + 2) × 3 adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: Which grouping of 5 × 6 × 2 makes a 10 first?
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, and 10 × 6 = 60 is easy. The other groupings with × give the same product, but with harder steps. (5 + 2) × 6 adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: 8 × 8 = (8 × 5) + (8 × 3). What is 8 × 8?
6 × 7 = (6 × 5) + (6 × 2). What is 6 × 7?
9 × 7 = (9 × 5) + (9 × 2). What is 9 × 7?
7 × 8 = (7 × 5) + (7 × 3). What is 7 × 8?

items.e: You can multiply in any order: 7 × 9 = 9 × 7. So ? = 7. Not 63: both sides must be equal, so ? is not the answer to 7 × 9.
Turn-around facts: 12 × 5 = 5 × 12. So ? = 5. Not 60: = means “the same as”, not “the answer is”.
Multiplication can be done in any order, so 5 × 9 = 9 × 5 is true. Division cannot: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 but 4 ÷ 20 is less than 1. 7 × 3 = 21, not 10. 6 × 4 = 24, not 144.

items.q: Work out 5 × 17 × 2. Hint: multiply the 5 and the 2 first.
items.e: Multiply 5 × 2 first: 5 × 2 = 10. Then 10 × 17 = 170. Not 85: that forgets the × 2.

items.e: Multiply 4 × 25 first: 4 × 25 = 100. Then 100 × 13 = 1 300. Not 325: that forgets the × 4.

items.q: Ravi bikes 8 km to Stanley Park and 8 km back home. In the park he rides a 9 km loop on the seawall. How far does he bike in all?
items.e: One expression: 2 × 8 + 9. 2 × 8 + 9 = 16 + 9 = 25, so 25 km. Not 34 km: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 17 km: that forgets the ride back home. Not 16 km: that stops one step too early.

items.q: Two soccer teams, with 11 and 13 players, share 72 orange slices equally. How many slices does each player get?
items.e: One expression: 72 ÷ (11 + 13). 72 ÷ (11 + 13) = 72 ÷ 24 = 3, so 3 slices. Not 48 slices: that subtracts instead of dividing. Not 36 slices: that shares between the 2 teams, not between the players. Not 24 slices: that is the number of players, not slices.

items.q: A lacrosse team has 3 cases of 24 water bottles. The coaches keep 8 bottles. The 16 players share the rest equally. How many bottles does each player get?
items.e: One expression: (3 × 24 − 8) ÷ 16. (3 × 24 − 8) ÷ 16 = (72 − 8) ÷ 16 = 64 ÷ 16 = 4, so 4 bottles. Not 64 bottles: that forgets to share among the players. Not 5 bottles: that adds the coaches’ bottles instead of taking them away. Not 72 bottles: that forgets the coaches and the sharing.

items.q: In a class maths game, a correct answer scores 5 points and a bonus question scores 10 points. Nadia gets 9 correct answers and 3 bonus questions. What is her score?
items.e: One expression: 9 × 5 + 3 × 10. 9 × 5 + 3 × 10 = 45 + 3 × 10 = 45 + 30 = 75, so 75 points. Not 480 points: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 720 points: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 45 points: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A SkyTrain has 4 cars with 30 seats in each car. There are 25 people sitting down. How many seats are empty?
items.e: One expression: 4 × 30 − 25. 4 × 30 − 25 = 120 − 25 = 95, so 95 seats. Not 20 seats: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 145 seats: that uses the wrong sign. Not 9 seats: that adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: A class orders 8 pizzas. Each pizza is cut into 8 slices. Each of the 30 learners eats 2 slices. How many slices are left?
items.e: One expression: 8 × 8 − 30 × 2. 8 × 8 − 30 × 2 = 64 − 30 × 2 = 64 − 60 = 4, so 4 slices. Not 68 slices: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 34 slices: that gives each learner only 1 slice. Not 64 slices: that stops one step too early.

items.q: Two classes, with 26 and 28 learners, make teams of 6 for a field day. Which expression gives the number of teams?
items.e: (26 + 28) ÷ 6 = 54 ÷ 6 = 9. So there are 9 teams. Brackets are needed: without them you would divide only the 28 by 6.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 4 987 × 21?
items.e: Round each number: 4 987 ≈ 5 000 and 21 ≈ 20. 5 000 × 20 = 100 000. (The exact answer is 104 727.) 10 000 and 1 000 000 have the wrong number of zeros. 150 000 rounds 21 to 30.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 6 213 − 2 890?
items.e: 6 213 ≈ 6 000 and 2 890 ≈ 3 000. 6 000 − 3 000 = 3 000. (The exact answer is 3 323.) 9 000 adds instead of subtracting. 4 000 rounds 2 890 down to 2 000.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 7 820 ÷ 39?
items.e: 7 820 ≈ 8 000 and 39 ≈ 40. 8 000 ÷ 40 = 800 ÷ 4 = 200. (The exact answer is about 200,5.) 2 000 and 20 have the wrong number of zeros. 160 rounds 39 to 50.

items.q: Johan works out 398 × 52 and gets 2 696. Use an estimate to check. What do you find?
c: It is wrong: the answer should be about 200 000
It is wrong: the answer should be about 20 000
It is right: the answer should be about 2 500
It is right: the answer should be about 2 000
items.e: 398 ≈ 400 and 52 ≈ 50. 400 × 50 = 20 000, so 2 696 is far too small. (The exact answer is 20 696; Johan has missed a zero when multiplying by the 5 tens.)

items.q: 1 030 people are going to a concert by coach. Each coach has 49 seats. How many coaches are needed?
items.e: 1 030 ÷ 49 = 21 remainder 1. 21 coaches carry 1 029 people, so 1 person still needs a seat. Round up: 22 coaches. 20 comes from the estimate 1 000 ÷ 50, which is not accurate enough here.

items.q: A café needs 200 eggs. Eggs come in boxes of 6. How many boxes must the café buy?
items.e: 200 ÷ 6 = 33 remainder 2. 33 boxes hold only 198 eggs, so the café needs one more box: 34 boxes. You cannot buy part of a box, so 33 r 2 and 33,3 do not make sense here.

items.q: Priya buys 4 packs of 6 pens and 3 single pens. Which calculation gives the number of pens?
items.e: 4 packs of 6 is 4 × 6, then add the 3 single pens: 4 × 6 + 3 = 24 + 3 = 27. 4 × (6 + 3) = 36 would mean 4 packs of 9.

items.q: Ofentse has 500 stickers. She gives 25 stickers to each of 8 friends. How many stickers does she have left?
items.e: 500 − 8 × 25 = 500 − 200 = 300. Multiply first. 12 300 comes from working left to right. 475 gives stickers to only one friend. 200 is the number given away.

items.q: A class has 18 boys and 14 girls. They sit in groups of 4. Which calculation gives the number of groups?
items.e: Find the whole class first, then divide by 4: (18 + 14) ÷ 4 = 32 ÷ 4 = 8 groups. Without brackets, 18 + 14 ÷ 4 would divide only the girls.

items.q: A stadium has 45 000 seats. 8 stands of 3 500 seats are full and every other seat is empty. How many seats are empty?
items.e: 45 000 − 8 × 3 500 = 45 000 − 28 000 = 17 000. 8 × 3 500 = 8 × 35 hundreds = 280 hundreds = 28 000. 41 500 counts only one stand. 28 000 is the number of full seats. 73 000 adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: A rectangular garden is 12 m by 8 m. A square patio with 4 m sides is laid in it. What area of the garden is left?
items.e: Area of garden − area of patio: 12 × 8 − 4<sup>2</sup> = 12 × 8 − 16 = 96 − 16 = 80 m². 88 m² uses 4<sup>2</sup> = 8 instead of 16. 92 m² takes away only 4. 96 m² forgets the patio.

items.q: A square patio is 6 slabs long and 6 slabs wide. 5 of the slabs are cracked. How many slabs are not cracked?
items.e: 6<sup>2</sup> − 5 = 36 − 5 = 31. 7 uses 6<sup>2</sup> = 12 instead of 36. 36 forgets the cracked slabs. 41 adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: 96 pencils are shared equally between 4 tables. Each table shares its pencils equally between 2 learners. How many pencils does each learner get?
items.e: 96 ÷ 4 ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12. 48 comes from working out 4 ÷ 2 first. 24 is the number for each table. 16 divides by 4 + 2 = 6.
